full_judgment:
Amirul Islam Chowdhury J.— This rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dacca, to show cause why the proceedings in G. R. Case No. 448/73 pending in the Court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Munshiganj should not be quashed. 

 That one Rustom Ali Madbar on 17-7-1973 lodged a First Information Report at Munshiganj Police Station under sections 148, 307, 326 and 114 of the Penal Code and P. O. 50/72 alleging that on 16-6-73 at about 9 P.M. the accused petitioners along with others being armed with deadly weapons attacked Hazrat Ali son of Rustom Ali Madbar and Sirajul Islam son of Subed Ali Mridha on the steps of the tank of Paikpara High School and accused petitioner Amirul alias Khokon by brush fire from the sten gun seriously injured both Hazrat Ali and Sirajul Islam. Both of them were given first aid by the local Doctor and thereafter were sent to Dacca. At Dacca they were admitted into Salimullah Medical College Hospital where both of them died on 17-7-73. Death of Hazrat Ali and Sirajul Islam took place after lodging of the F.I.R. G. R. Case No. 448/73 was started in the Court of the Sub-divisional Magistrate, Munshiganj. After completing investigation the Police submitted charge sheet No. 10 dated 10. 6. 74 against the accused petitioners and others on 24. 6. 74 under sections 146/302/34 B.P.C. and P.O. 50/72. The petitioners on 12-2-75 moved this Court for quashing the proceedings and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Mr. Abdul Hye Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners has contended that the proceeding in the instant, case where charge sheet was not submitted before 9-2-74, the date on which P.O. 50/72 Was repealed cannot be continued as the said proceeding has not been saved by Saving clause of the repealing Act, namely, Special Powers Act and as such the proceeding is liable to be quashed. Mr. Choudhury further contended that since the Special Powers Act that by section 36(2) (b) has provided for the continuance of only the "pending cases" under the repealed Statute, i.e. P. O. 50 of 1972; the legislature apparently did not intend to keep alive any proceedings other than the "Pending cases" as mentioned in section 36(2) (b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974. The intention of the legislature being clear that no proceeding except the "pending case" to be kept alive, the provision of the General Clause Act, 1897 would be inapplicable in the present case. In this connection he referred to the case of Public Prosecutor, Government of Pendichari Vs. Abdul Aziz Khan and another, reported in A.I.R. 1970 (Mad)-311. Mr. Chowdhury has next submitted that in a case in which charge sheet was not submitted and investigation was still in progress it was not pending case within the meaning of Section 36(2) (b) of the Special Powers Act and in support of his contention he relied on the decision of the Appellate Division of this Court in the case of solicitor, Government of Bangladesh Vs. A.T. Mridha, reported in 26 D.L.R. 17. Mr. Chowdhury has also submitted that if after 9-2-74 the Police on investigation finds a prima facie case against the accused-petitioned, charge sheet cannot be submitted under P. O. 50/72 and in this connection he relied on the cases of Tofazzal Hossain Sardar and others Vs. The State and Abu Tayab Md. Mashood and Tipu Vs. the State reported respectively at page 36 and 93 in 27 D.L.R. 

 4. Mr. Moazzem Hossain, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the State submitted that the Saving Clause, i.e. Section 36(2)(b) of the Special Powers Act does not specifically include cases like the proceeding in question, such proceedings have been saved and kept alive by section 6(e) of the General Clause Act, 1897. He did not dispute that the present proceeding on the date of the announcement of the Special Powers Act was not a "Pending case" within the meaning of section 36(2)(b) of the said Act. He, however, submitted that section 6(e) of the General Clause Act is sufficient enough to show that any investigation or legal proceeding started under the Statute will not be affected by the subsequent repeal of the Statute unless a different intention appears in the repealing Statute. He contended that section 6(e) of the General Clauses Act will be applicable in the present case inasmuch as section 36(2)(b) of the Special Powers Act does not contain any different intention, and as such the instant proceeding has been kept alive despite the repeal of P. O. 50/72. In support of his contention, he relied on the case of Baliah Vs. Rangachari, Income Tax Officer, reported in A.I.R. 1969 (S.C.) 701; Wherein it has been held that "different intention" means intention to destroy a legal proceedings or investigation taking under the repealed statute before its repeal. In support of his contention that inspire of the Saving Clause i.e. section 36(2)(b) of the Special Powers Act, proceeding other than" pending Cases" has been saved by virtue of section 6(e) of the General Clause Act. Mr. Moazzem Hossain referred to 3 unreported decisions of this Court, one Criminal Misc. Case No. 84(74 (Shyamal Cas & others Vs. the State and (2) Criminal Revision No. 470/74 Sabje Ali and another Vs. the state and (3) Criminal Revision No. 584/74 (A.K. Rabbani alias Salim Vs. the State. In the aforesaid 3 cases relied on by Mr. Moazzem Hossain their Lordships considered sections 36(2)(b) Special Powers Act, and section 6(e) of the General Clauses Act. In all the 3 cases the question as to whether in view of section 36(2)(b) of the Special Powers Act any other proceeding except 'pending cases' mentioned in that section of the Special Powers Act has been saved after repeal of P. O. 50/72; has been considered at length and it has been held in the said case that such proceedings have been saved in spite of saving clause provided in section 36(2)(b) of the Special Powers Act, by virtue of section 6(e) of the General Clause Act. We have also in Criminal Revision No. 1871/74 (Akhtar Hossain & others Vs. the State) agreed with the view expressed in this decision. We do not find any reason to deviate from the principles laid down in the decision referred to above. We are, therefore, of the opinion that investigation or proceedings started under P.O. 50/72 will be continued under the provisions of the said Act (P.O. 50/72) by virtue of section 6(e) of the General Clauses Act in spite of the repeal of P.O.50/72 and the saving clause relating to only "pending casks" in section 36(2)(b) of the Special Powers Act, repealing the Act. 

 5. As regards the 2 cases reported in 27 D.L.R. at pages 36 and 93 referred to by Mr. Chowdhury, it may be observed that the same Bench which decided the aforesaid 2 cases subsequently while deciding Criminal Misc. Case No. 84/74 referred to above by Mr. Moazzem Hossain came to the finding that despite the repeal of P.O.50/72, the proceedings started therein will continue. It is thus apparent that the observations made in the above 2 cases reported in 27 D.L.R. at pages 36 and 93 have clearly been over ruled by the later decision of the same Bench in Criminal Misc. case No. 84/74. 

 Let the records of the case be sent down to the learned Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Munshiganj with direction for disposal of the case expeditiously.
